subject: general
question: Why is it generally more severe to be burnt by steam at 100°C than by boiling water at 100°C?

options.text: Steam is hotter than boiling water.
Steam contains more latent heat of vaporization.
Steam has a higher specific heat capacity.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Steam contains more latent heat of vaporization.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• Steam at 100°C contains additional energy in the form of latent heat of vaporization, which is the energy required to convert water into steam without changing its temperature.
 
• This latent heat of vaporization is released when steam condenses on the skin, transferring a large amount of heat energy, causing more severe burns compared to boiling water.&
